tob-10078: Quaker scholar Rufus Jones profiles the spiritual reformers of early modern Europe. He writes about figures such as the German mystic Jacob Boehme and the French quietist Madame Guyon, who sought a deeper inward religion during the age of religious wars. Their teachings offered an alternative to the bitter doctrinal fights of their time. The book helped revive scholarly interest in these overlooked figures.
tob-4178: Saadi’s Gulistan — the Rose-plot — is Persia’s dearest wisdom-book, mingling prose tales with verse on kings, holy beggars, and life’s conduct. Penned in 1258, it schooled generations of readers. Its saws are quoted through the Persian world. Boston’s 1865 printing bore it to American readers.
cia-0000119578: An April 1966 special report from the Current Intelligence Weekly on the Czechoslovak party's problems — the truncated title cuts off the rest. Prague's communists were struggling with economic failure and rising dissent. Two years before the Prague Spring, the cracks were already showing — and being reported.
cia-0000126978: The National Intelligence Bulletin's Angola edition, dated June 1975 — the day's essential reading on the coming civil war. Three liberation movements, two superpowers, and one oil-rich prize. The document is the Angola crisis distilled for the president's morning.
cia-0000132178: Situation Report 494: the Soviets evacuating their people as the war intensified — the truncated title suggests the rest. Moscow was pulling its citizens out of the battle zone. The document marks the superpower stepping back from its client's war.
cia-0000126878: An estimated August 1968 study of the short-run economic effects of the Soviet occupation of Czechoslovakia. Invasion economics: disrupted factories, frightened markets, immediate costs. The document measures what the tanks did to the economy in their first weeks — before the long occupation's bill came due.
cia-0000132278: Situation Report 587: Spanish legislators reaffirming support for the UN effort — the truncated title suggests the rest. Holding the coalition meant constant reassurance, vote by vote. The document is democracy's contribution: a parliament, on record, for the war.
cia-0000132578: Item 11 in the September 1960 series: Castro evidently planning a return to the UN General Assembly. The Cuban leader's New York visits were theater — the famous 1960 stay included. The document anticipates the performance: the podium, awaiting its star.
cia-0000132678: A 1961 item: Poland continuing long-term credits to Cuba — and a Latin America fragment, the truncated title suggests. Warsaw's loans kept Havana afloat. The document is the credit: the Poles, lending.
cia-0000135978: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN exploring the possibility of trading a burnt plane. A charred aircraft was a bargaining chip — or an embarrassment to unload. The document is the deal: the wreck, offered.
cia-0000136278: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for LANGEVIN with instruction 15 for broadcast. The airwaves campaign, nearing its numbered end. The entry is the instruction: the broadcast, directed — number fifteen.
cia-0000138978: A 1946 military information report on Russian troop dispositions. The armies, placed. The document is the map: the troops, positioned.
un-ga-res-a-69-78: Resolution A/69/78, cataloged with the year 1995 — session and year disagree. The designation is preserved; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1378: Security Council Resolution 1378, adopted in November 2001 — the Afghanistan resolution, supporting international efforts to establish a new transitional government as the Taliban fell. The Council blessed the Bonn process. The resolution is the endorsement: the transition, supported.
un-sc-res-1478: Security Council Resolution 1478, cataloged with the year 2001 — the numbering suggests 2003, a mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted.
un-sc-res-1678: Security Council Resolution 1678, cataloged with the year 2005 — the numbering suggests 2006, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-1778: Security Council Resolution 1778, adopted in September 2007 — the Chad and Central African Republic resolution, authorizing a European Union force and a UN mission to protect refugees from the Darfur spillover. The Council answered a regional crisis. The resolution is the protection: the refugees, guarded.
un-sc-res-1878: Security Council Resolution 1878, adopted in 2009 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
cia-0000132778: A 1960 CIA file on Cuba and the Caribbean, numbered 0000132778. The wider view of the revolutionary moment. The document is the view: the moment, widened.
cia-0000135678: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135678. The training year's paper trail. The entry is the trail: the brigade, on paper.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d78: President Roosevelt to Generalissimo Chiang, October 30, 1943 — Document 78. The president wrote China's leader. The message is the fourth ally: Chiang, addressed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d178: United States delegation minutes of the final meeting of the Moscow Conference — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 178. The last session, minuted. The minutes are the finale: the conference, closed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d278: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 278. The editors' bridge. The note is the bridge: the narrative, continuous.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d378: Bohlen minutes, December 1, 1943 — Document 378. A second minuting that day. The minutes are the second: Bohlen, again.
a-history-of-modern-europe-1792-1878: Charles Alan Fyffe's history carries Europe from the French Revolution through the unification of Germany — the age of Napoleon, nationalism, and empire. Clear narrative and sound judgment made it a standard English textbook for decades. Students meeting the making of modern Europe for the first time will find it a reliable guide.
chantry-house-pg7378: Charlotte Yonge's Chantry House — an old home, its ghosts of the past, and the family within. Her last great novel of English country life. Yonge's world at its most complete. Old Colonel Keith and young Grisel tell their stories with Yonge's best art.
arxiv-2605-08778: Attackers rarely break a chatbot's safeguards with a single message; they wear it down across many turns of conversation. Zhida He and colleagues dissect multi-turn jailbreaking through credit assignment, asking which turns in the dialogue actually did the damage. The 2026 paper is AI-safety research: understanding the slow-burn attack is the first step to closing it.
arxiv-2605-08878: Even carefully aligned chatbots can be jailbroken, and Yu Chen and Yuanhao Liu dig into why. The paper traces jailbreaks to refusal-escape directions — paths in the model's inner space that dodge its trained refusal — and to operator-level sources of the weakness. It is AI-safety research that treats jailbreaking as a structural property, not a mere bug.
arxiv-2605-08978: AI agents that reason step by step tend to exploit what already works instead of exploring what might. Xingyuan Hua, Sheng Yue, and Ju Ren propose exploration-aware policy optimization, rewarding the agent for searching as well as solving. The 2026 paper scales agentic reasoning by teaching curiosity.
arxiv-2605-09078: W2246-0526 is one of the most luminous obscured quasars known — a monster black hole hidden behind dust. Charalambia Varnava, Andreas Efstathiou, Tanio Díaz-Santos, and colleagues combine JWST observations with a model of the beast. The 2026 paper peers through the dust at a cosmic powerhouse.
arxiv-2605-09178: Contact Lie algebras encode the geometry of odd-dimensional spaces with a distinguished hyperplane field; the centerless unimodular ones are a special breed. Agustín Garrone studies them and their structure. The 2026 paper is pure Lie theory on a refined class of algebras.
arxiv-2605-09578: Implanting nitrogen into gallium oxide — a promising wide-bandgap semiconductor — can form molecular nitrogen trapped inside the crystal. I.N. Demchenko, Y. Syryanyy, A. Shokri, and colleagues study the formation process. The 2026 paper is materials science for next-generation electronics.
arxiv-2605-09878: Ergotropy — the maximum work extractable from a quantum state — meets Clifford operations, the efficiently simulable gates. Somnath Maity and Ryusuke Hamazaki study Clifford ergotropy. The 2026 paper is quantum thermodynamics on exactly what Clifford circuits can squeeze out of quantum states today.
plos-pone-0003378: Pathologists gained a better way to stain preserved brain tissue in this 2008 methods study. Finding a specific protein, an antigen, in decades-old human brain samples had been difficult for thirty years. Their new antigen-retrieval technique makes hidden targets visible again, strengthening a key tool for studying brain disease in archived tissue.
plos-pone-0003478: Theorists built a mathematical model of a stem cell's identity crisis in this 2008 paper. The transcription factors Oct4, Sox2, and Nanog form a self-reinforcing network that keeps embryonic stem cells undecided, and the model shows how that network tips cells toward staying stem-like or becoming trophectoderm or endoderm. The equations capture the logic of life's earliest choices.
plos-pone-0003578: Gut-disease researchers fingered a bacterial suspect in children's intestinal biopsies in this 2008 paper. Using 16S ribosomal DNA, a universal bacterial barcode, they identified and characterized Pseudomonas species in the ileum. The microbial census adds evidence that the gut flora's composition may shape inflammatory bowel disease in young patients.
plos-pone-0003678: In 2008, Proekt, Wong, and Zhurov linked brain dynamics to smart behavior. Since the nervous system stays coupled to its surroundings, the team showed which dynamical properties let an animal act adaptively in a changing world. The work reads behavior straight from the physics of brain-environment coupling.
plos-pone-0003778: Woodland and Fry traced the ancestry of centrioles in this 2008 paper. Their wide survey of Pix proteins, core parts of the cell's organizing centers, mapped who has them and how flagella fit in. The evolutionary census clarifies how these ancient structures diversified.
plos-pone-0003878: In 2008, a team sequenced a microbe that shrugs off nuclear waste. Kineococcus radiotolerans, pulled from a radioactive site in South Carolina, survived gamma rays nearly as well as the famous Deinococcus. Its genome revealed the tricks of extreme resistance, with hints for cleaning up toxic sites.
plos-pone-0003978: In 2008, Nestor, Vettel, and Tarr asked how the job changes face reading. Detecting a face versus identifying one used different neural codes for facial features. The task at hand reshaped how the brain represented the very same face. The finding shows face perception is not fixed but tuned to purpose.
plos-pone-0004078: In 2008, Wang and Vavylonis modeled how yeast cells grow their cables. Their model of For3p-mediated actin cable assembly ran in fission yeast. The formin protein nucleates cables at cell tips for polarized growth. The math turns microscope hints into a working mechanism.
plos-pone-0004178: In 2009, Ihm, Sparks, and Lee modeled a viral shuttle's shape. Their structural model of the Rev regulatory protein came from equine infectious anemia virus. Rev ferries unfinished viral messages out of the nucleus. The shape guides drugs that jam the shuttle.
plos-pone-0004278: In 2009, Beaslas, Cueille, and Delers found gut cells tasting dietary fat. Enterocytes sensed dietary lipids through SR-BI/CLA-1. The fat sensor tuned triglyceride-rich lipoprotein release. The finding maps the gut's lipid radar. The sensor could be a target for cholesterol drugs.
plos-pone-0358778: A C-section can save mother and baby — but in Tamil Nadu, India, it can also wreck a family’s finances. This paper measured the financial burden and quality-of-life impact on post-partum mothers after caesarean deliveries. The findings put numbers on a hidden cost of surgical birth in a setting where most families pay out of pocket.
plos-pone-0357278: Predicting how tightly a drug molecule grips its protein target is the first step in drug design. This paper presents RA-PLA, a method that pairs graph neural networks with a retrieval system — borrowing lessons from similar known drug-protein pairs. The combination predicts binding strength more accurately than either technique alone.
plos-pone-0343078: Gut bacteria may influence type 1 diabetes, and young donors’ microbes could be the healthiest reset available. This paper publishes the protocol for a pilot randomized trial testing youth-derived fecal microbiota transplantation in adults with type 1 diabetes. Laying out safety and feasibility plans in advance sets the stage for an unusual but promising therapy.
plos-pone-0355678: Who supports political violence in America — and why? This national survey linked party affiliation, ideology, and views on democracy and society to support for political violence in the United States. The findings map the country’s fault lines with unusual candor, showing which beliefs predict a willingness to endorse force.
plos-pone-0358078: Dialysis patients who need knee replacements face compounded surgical risks. This nationwide propensity score-matched analysis studied inpatient outcomes after primary total knee arthroplasty in chronic dialysis patients. The results quantify the added danger — hard numbers to inform the agonizing go/no-go decision.
plos-pone-0357778: Stored sorghum feeds families for months — unless weevils eat the stores first. This laboratory evaluation tested plant powders against the maize weevil in stored sorghum. The botanical results offer smallholder farmers cheap, locally available protection for their precious grain reserves.
plos-pone-0357478: Jewish college students navigate campus life amid rising antisemitism and political tension. This study examined the well-being of Jewish college students in the United States. The findings document both the pressures they face and their resilience — with clear implications for campus support services.
plos-pone-0356878: Network intruders hate tamper-proof logs they cannot erase. This paper built a lightweight blockchain-inspired hybrid intrusion detection system with ensemble learning for tamper-proof auditing. The hybrid design catches attacks in progress while keeping the audit trail itself trustworthy and unalterable.
plos-pone-0357578: Spotting lymph node spread in bile duct cancer determines how surgeons operate. This paper tested the coefficient of variation of CT values for predicting lymph node metastasis in extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The image-based metric gives surgeons a preoperative clue about how far the cancer has traveled.
plos-pone-0355778: Ebola’s scars outlast the virus by years. This study examined fear, stigma, and uncertainty among survivors, affected families, and entire communities in Bundibugyo, western Uganda — in both the short and long term. The firsthand accounts demand far better support for those the outbreak left behind.
plos-pone-0335578: Estimating tree volume and biomass demands equations built for the local forest. This paper developed allometric equations for Acacia mangium on the Batéké Plateau in the Republic of the Congo. The equations give foresters and carbon accountants trustworthy numbers for this fast-growing plantation species.
plos-pone-0356178: Children’s immune responses to COVID-19 vaccination differ meaningfully from adults’. This comparative analysis examined age-specific humoral immune responses — antibody levels in children versus adults after primary vaccination series or infection. The differences carry direct implications for pediatric dosing strategies.
plos-pone-0355478: Do we conform to AI the way we conform to other humans? This paper studied conformity to AI versus humans, testing social exclusion and task type as moderating factors. The findings reveal when — and why — machines sway our judgments, with implications for everything from chatbots to automated hiring.
plos-pone-0356478: After a drug-eluting stent is placed, re-narrowing — restenosis — remains the feared complication. This paper tested the predictive value of the non-HDL to HDL cholesterol ratio for in-stent restenosis. The simple ratio refines risk prediction, helping cardiologists spot vulnerable patients earlier.
plos-pone-0355978: When toxic algae bloom, shrimp pay the price in their hepatopancreas — the digestive powerhouse. This transcriptome analysis examined the hepatopancreas of whiteleg shrimp (Litopenaeus vannamei) after acute exposure to Alexandrium pacificum. The gene expression changes reveal exactly how the algal toxin attacks, guiding aquaculture defenses.
plos-pone-0354678: Real-time weight monitoring could transform behavioral weight loss — but the physiology needs understanding first. The ADAPT study protocol outlines assessing the physiology of weight loss using continuous weight data. The planned research will reveal how bodies actually respond, day by day, to sustained weight loss efforts.
plos-pone-0342878: What evidence actually supports new drug approvals — and is it changing? This paper tracked the changes in evidence used for FDA Novel Drug Approvals from 2016 to 2024. The eight-year trend analysis reveals whether the gold standard of drug evidence is holding firm or quietly eroding.
plos-pone-0356378: Measuring iron inside mouse brain tumors — in living animals versus excised tissue — demands method comparison. This paper compared in vivo and ex vivo iron quantification methods. The validated approaches let cancer researchers track iron’s role in tumor biology with confidence.
plos-pone-0354978: Predicting healthcare costs for older adults requires models validated on real data. This paper externally validated a cost-prediction model using both cohort-derived and claims-derived predictors in community-dwelling older adults. The validation tells health systems which data sources genuinely forecast spending.
plos-pone-0354878: Diffusion bonding joins metals without melting — but joint strength depends on process parameters. This paper optimized parameters for enhancing tensile strength in diffusion-bonded Al–Al and Al–Fe–Al laminates. The optimized bonding produces joints strong enough for demanding structural applications.
plos-pone-0351878: Massage for cancer patients — soothing or risky? This systematic review and meta-analysis examined the harms of massage in persons with cancer or receiving treatment. The synthesized evidence gives oncologists and therapists the safety data to guide touch-based comfort care without causing harm.
plos-pone-0355278: Children needing critical care and surgery — the barriers their families face are often invisible to the system. This qualitative study explored those barriers to accessing paediatric critical care and surgery. The families’ accounts demand health systems designed around their realities, not institutional convenience.
europmc-pmc2816178: Primary microcephaly, a condition where babies are born with small brains, can stem from several different genes. This 2009 review asks whether all these genetic roads lead to the same biological mechanism. The authors weigh the evidence for a shared pathway. The synthesis helped focus the search for what unites these diverse genetic causes.
europmc-pmc2848978: Tiny RNAs fade with age, and this 2010 paper measures the decline. The authors show miR-17, miR-19b, miR-20a, and miR-106a are down-regulated in human aging. Their profiling across ages reveals a consistent pattern. The signature offers candidate biomarkers for biological age.
europmc-pmc2868878: Stepping into a virtual body can feel eerily real. This 2010 paper reports first-person experiments of body transfer in virtual reality. The authors show people can feel ownership of a digital body. Their work opened a window on how the brain builds the sense of self.
europmc-pmc2873978: Genes get all the focus in diabetes, but surroundings matter too. This 2010 paper runs an environment-wide association study on type 2 diabetes, scanning life exposures the way gene studies scan DNA. The authors' sweep found links between everyday exposures and the disease. Their approach gave the environment the same hard look that genes have long enjoyed.
europmc-pmc2936378: Paying doctors for performance sounds sensible, but does it work? This 2010 systematic review weighs the effects, design choices, and context of pay-for-performance in health care. The authors find mixed results across programs. Their review tempers enthusiasm with hard evidence.
europmc-pmc2944278: COPD is many diseases wearing one name, and this 2010 paper sorts them out. The authors characterize COPD heterogeneity in the big ECLIPSE cohort of patients. Their subtypes point toward personalized lung care. The work moved COPD beyond one-size-fits-all treatment.
europmc-pmc3014878: Pregnancy and its dangerous complication shift immune signals. This 2010 paper measures blood immune signals in healthy pregnancy and preeclampsia. The authors reveal the shifts. Their work points to early warning markers. Catching preeclampsia early saves two lives. The signal panel may become a routine test.
europmc-pmc3044678: Tree youth is held by tiny RNAs. This 2011 paper shows small RNAs keep trees in their juvenile phase. The authors reveal the youth switch. Their work aids forestry. Juvenile trees root cuttings far better. Foresters flip the switch to clone winners.
europmc-pmc6535078: Age is the strongest risk factor for ischemic stroke - the blockage-driven kind - shaping who suffers one and how they recover. This review examines the intersection: how aging blood vessels, hearts, and brains raise stroke risk, and why older patients face tougher recoveries. Understanding age's role helps doctors tailor prevention and treatment across the lifespan.
europmc-pmc6598278: Parkinson's may start in the gut: patients show shifted gut bacteria and matching immune signals. Studying people in Taiwan, researchers linked specific microbial changes to inflammatory cytokine responses in Parkinson's disease. The gut-brain connection strengthens the case that the disease's roots reach far beyond the brain.
europmc-pmc6650278: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis arise from a three-way collision: genes, immunity, and gut microbes. This landmark multi-omics study profiled all three layers in IBD patients - microbes, metabolites, and host signals together. The integrated map reveals how microbial shifts track with flare-ups.
europmc-pmc6656778: Genome scans flag thousands of DNA variants linked to traits - but which ones actually do something? This study merges GWAS hits with gene-expression data (eQTLs) using Mendelian randomization, a genetics trick that mimics trials. The integration pins down causal genes behind complex traits.
gao-gaoreports-b-299978: A 2007 GAO ruling on three linked contract fights from AlliedBarton Security Services LLC. The guard giant challenged a trio of federal awards; the ruling works the claims one by one. The call shows GAO juggling repeat filings from a heavyweight of the hired-guard trade — and keeping each bid on its own merits.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1078: Flood insurance money was leaking to middlemen in 2007 — GAO's report says FEMA's watch over payments to private insurers needed muscle. The findings question whether the firms selling federal flood policies earned their cut. In a program already drowning in red ink, every wasted dollar stung twice.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-678: The money cops were grading themselves in 2007 — GAO's report says the financial regulators had adopted key performance habits, with room to grow further. The findings measure the measurers against best practice. The report's gentle prod: even regulators need report cards of their own.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-578: The Pentagon's spy eyes needed joining up in 2007 — GAO's report says its intelligence and surveillance systems could share more and waste less. The findings target the stovepipes. The report's vision: one picture from many sensors, not many pictures from one war.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-478: Wetland permits bought with outside cash drew GAO's eye in 2007 — the report says the Corps needed to keep those decisions clean. The findings probe the funding influence. The report's principle: a permit is a public trust, not a purchased favor.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-278: The visitor-tracking program's budget needed justifying in 2007, and GAO's report says the planned spending had to be adequately defined. The findings demand the details. The report warns that the border's digital eye should not be bought blind. The dollars had to match the mission.
openalex-w4412745578: Python powers modern labs, and this paper shows how one lab uses it. The authors shared real examples: crunching data and automating boring tasks in Python. They pitched its ease for scientists. A friendly how-to paper straight from the lab bench.
openalex-w7204994078: After colon surgery, how the bowel is tucked back may matter. This trial of 160 patients tested whether small-intestine arrangement affects gut function after laparoscopic colectomy. The team compared the new layout against standard care. A surgical study of plumbing details with real consequences.
pmc-13449878: A 2026 immunology theory paper asking a deceptively simple question: what does the "shape space" of T cell epitopes — the small protein fragments immune cells recognize — actually look like? Mapping the geometry of what T cells can see has deep implications for vaccine design. The paper offers a mathematical portrait of immune recognition.
pmc-13554778: This 2026 cardiology paper reports on paclitaxel-coated balloons — drug-delivering angioplasty balloons — for coronary in-stent restenosis and new lesions in Chinese patients. Coated balloons treat re-narrowed arteries without adding another stent layer. The study adds population-specific evidence for the technique.
pmc-13326778: A 2026 systematic review on the effectiveness of nature-based interventions for mental health. Green time is widely prescribed but the evidence needed synthesis. The review grades what nature exposure actually delivers.
pmc-13482278: In this 2026 (listed 2025) bovine embryology paper, in vitro processes altered the epigenome and transcriptome of the embryonic disc in pre-implantation elongated embryos. Lab culture leaves molecular marks. The finding matters for assisted reproduction in cattle.
pmc-13551778: In this 2026 cancer paper, extracellular vesicle-transferred miR-7111-3p inhibited malignant phenotypes and tumor growth in nasopharyngeal carcinoma by targeting APP-regulated epithelial-mesenchymal transition. The vesicle-delivered microRNA is a natural tumor suppressor. The mechanism is the discovery.
pmc-13467578: A 2026 Kazakh retrospective cohort study of survival, disability, and neurorehabilitation after advanced endovascular stroke care. The Central Asian data fill a geographic gap. The outcomes inform regional stroke systems.
pmc-13580678: A 2026 paper on metabolic exhaustion, p38 MAPK/Rac1/MLKL signaling, and calcium influx mediating solasodine-triggered eryptosis — red blood cell suicide. The plant compound's kill mechanism was mapped. The pathway is the discovery.
pmc-13529578: A 2026 correction notice for a paper on calibrated non-inferiority margins accounting for population shift in stroke trials. Corrections amend the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13517478: In this 2026 nephrology paper, indoxyl sulfate-mediated blood-brain barrier damage in chronic kidney disease was studied. The gut-derived toxin breached the brain's defenses. The mechanism links kidney failure to cognitive decline.
pmc-13501278: A 2026 paper finding a spectrum of gut microbiota signatures predicts long-term health status. The microbiome forecasted the future. The predictive spectrum is the claim.
pmc-13469878: A 2026 paper on unilateral bi-portal endoscopic spinal surgery for lumbar disk herniation and canal stenosis — technical nuances and fellowship-based clinical experience (the title is truncated). The minimally invasive spine technique was detailed. The experience is the teaching.
pmc-13469178: In this 2026 stroke paper, urolithin A exerted neuroprotective effects against ischemic stroke by inhibiting oxidative stress and neuroinflammation. The gut-derived metabolite protected the brain. The inhibition is the mechanism.
pmc-13468078: A 2026 special issue, second edition, on metabolic features and nutritional interventions in chronic diseases. The nutrition-disease interface was updated. The edition is the collection.
pmc-13449178: A 2026 paper on the impact of bone marrow involvement on hematopoietic stem cell mobilization success in lymphoma patients. The marrow's disease burden affected collection. The impact guides apheresis planning.
pmc-13448078: A 2026 mouse study showing targeting of pentraxin 3 alleviated angiotensin II-induced cardiac hypertrophy. The immune protein's blockade protected the heart. The alleviation is the therapeutic hint.
pmc-13464278: A 2026 radiology piece, "Imaging the Answer." The images told the story. The entry is the case-based teaching.
pmc-13428078: A 2026 US study of early-onset gastric cancer as a high-risk disease entity — clinicopathologic features, regional variation, and outcomes. The young patients' cancer was profiled. The features reveal the threat.
pmc-13427878: A 2026 neonatal neurosurgery paper: prolonged puncturing decreased ventriculoperitoneal shunt insertion rates in neonates with posthemorrhagic ventricular dilatation. The repeated taps avoided shunts. The decrease is the clinical win.
pmc-13405178: A 2026 US study of mortality trends in heart failure patients with psychoactive substance abuse — pre- and post-COVID-19 pandemic perspective from 1999 (the title is truncated). The mortality trends were charted. The perspective reveals the pandemic's toll.
pmc-13462278: A 2026 paper assessing pesticide compatibility with entomopathogenic fungi for biological control — evidence from in vivo and in vitro assays. The chemical-biological compatibility was tested. The evidence guides integrated pest management.
pmc-13384778: A 2026 biochemistry paper on zinc-mediated structural and functional regulation of ERp44 and ERGIC-53 in protein quality control. The zinc's chaperone regulation was detailed. The regulation is the mechanism.
pmc-13427778: This 2026 pilot study showed international comparison of neutrophil surface markers after severe trauma was feasible using point-of-care flow cytometry. The bedside immune profiling worked across sites. The feasibility is the foundation.
pmc-13526478: A 2026 case report and literature review of proptosis revealing a neurological form of IgG4-related disease. The bulging eye unmasked the systemic disease. The case teaches the differential.
pmc-13475378: This 2026 case report described sporadic abdominopelvic neurofibroma presenting with genitourinary symptoms. The unusual tumor's presentation was documented. The case is the rarity.
pmc-13464378: This 2026 mouse study showed early amyloid pathology synergistically worsened post-sepsis behavioral impairment and microglial synaptic phagocytosis. The Alzheimer's-sepsis interaction was the danger. The worsening is the mechanistic insight.
pmc-13448478: A 2026 review of neuroimaging biomarkers of non-invasive brain stimulation in post-stroke recovery — EEG and fMRI perspectives. The stimulation's brain signatures were surveyed. The review guides neurorehabilitation.
pmc-13426078: A 2026 Paris-region cross-sectional study of prevalence, perceived effects, and motivations for adolescent e-cigarette use. The teens' vaping was surveyed. The motivations inform prevention.
pmc-13436078: In this 2026 protocol, a systematic review and meta-analysis of non-pharmacological interventions for lactational mastitis was planned. The protocol is the plan. The review will synthesize the evidence.
pmc-13481078: This 2026 optics paper derived sensitivity factors for diffuse optics — equations for finite changes. The light-tissue math was formalized. The derivation serves biomedical imaging.
arxiv-2606-16178: Robots that learn to move from camera images (visuomotor policies) tend to forget too fast for long tasks. This paper scales up their short-term memory so they can handle extended sequences — like an assembly job with many steps. It is robotics research on giving learned controllers a longer attention span for long-horizon work.
arxiv-2606-16378: Einstein's rulebook has a twin take — one-book gravity — with a fresh slant on the dark-push term. This paper bends that twin wider and tracks how babe ripples, the seeds of star-isles, wobble in it. For sky-rule testers. A clean what-if for cosmos doubters.
arxiv-2606-16578: The heat equation describes how temperature spreads, and "walk on spheres" is a clever random-walk method for solving it. This paper extends the idea to "heat stars" for parabolic equations with Neumann boundary conditions — insulated edges where heat can't escape. It targets numerical analysts and applied mathematicians.
arxiv-2606-16678: Pop-a-leaper fares steer chem — yet true fares cost dear. This paper stretches the Koopmans yard to hand those fares at mean-field price: thrifty sums, sound fares. For chem-code crews who need true pop fares on a dime. Dime fares, dear truths.
arxiv-2606-16778: Can AI fake being a human study volunteer? This paper compares real people with LLM-simulated participants on a writing-style task. The goal: learn where simulated volunteers match humans — and where they don't. It is for researchers who run studies with AI stand-ins.
